notes.claim: the README says the reports and holidays E2E suites are ones "this area does not touch and which must stay green"; the holidays E2E suite pins the very rule REQ-01-026 drops and cannot stay green untouched

witness.detail: e2e/tests/holidays.spec.ts:296-338 (TC-03-E2E-04) seeds a holiday with countryCode 'BY', calls setOwnCountryViaApi(request, 'BY') at :309 — which writes Account.phoneCountryCode — and then asserts `time-cell-{day}-holiday-marker` is visible on the weekly calendar. Under REQ-01-026 that member has no Membership.countryCode and the organization has none either, so the chain resolves null, GET /holidays?scope=mine returns global rows only, and the marker is not drawn. Three integration cases are in the same position: apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts:381 (fixture at :402), apps/api/test/reports-amounts-owed.spec.ts:573 and :607, and apps/api/test/reports-time-off.spec.ts:404.

notes.suggestedFix: the sentence should say the four cases move their fixture from the phone to the stated column while every assertion stands — filed as a note rather than a blocker because the product rule is stated completely (the contracts' call-site table: 'No call site keeps a phone-country read') and the repair is mechanical; it is planned as T10, a task of its own so the edits read as deliberate

notes.claim: whether a two-letter code that is not an assigned ISO country ('XX') is accepted by the two country writes has two readings

witness.detail: PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country with { "countryCode": "XX" }. REQ-01-036 refuses anything "neither empty nor a valid alpha-2 value", and Edge case 10 defines "XX" as a value that does not normalize to a valid alpha-2 value — so 422. The contracts' Validation Rule 9 states the constraint as "Empty, or exactly 2 uppercase letters" and the note under the table says the rule is the one "the holiday rows' country validator already does", which is validateHolidayCountryCode (packages/validation/src/holidays.ts:93, test /^[A-Z]{2}$/) — so 200. No case exercises it.

notes.suggestedFix: one clause saying whether the write checks membership of the ISO list or only the two-uppercase-letters shape. Planned as the Validation Rules table states it (validateHolidayCountryCode on both writes), since that table is the normative statement of what each write refuses and the read side skips a stored 'XX' regardless (REQ-01-027)

notes.claim: the case says a user and a viewer "receive the identical body" from the member detail read, and the shipped projection carries caller-dependent fields, so a literal reading of that clause cannot pass

witness.detail: MembersService.getDetail returns callerRole, canEditRole and availableRoles (apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:352-374); callerRole is 'user' for one caller and 'viewer' for the other, so a deep-equality assertion between the two bodies fails on a field this spec does not touch. The rest of the sentence says what is meant — "field included: the read is gated by no capability and the field is not conditional on one".

notes.suggestedFix: narrow the clause to the field the case is about. Planned as: countryCode present and equal for both callers, alongside the target-derived fields; no product code differs between the two readings

notes.rule: reviewer — two writes of one field disagree on what an absent key means, and only one of them wrote the decision down
notes.claim: on the organization country PUT an absent countryCode key clears the stored value, while the member update beside it deliberately treats an absent key as no submission at all

witness.detail: An admin has stored PL. A caller sends PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country with body {}. organization-country.service.ts:69 evaluates validateHolidayCountryCode(undefined), which returns { valid: true, value: null } (packages/validation/src/holidays.ts:96), and the update writes countryCode: null. The response is 200 {"countryCode":null} and every member relying on the organization link drops to global holidays only. REQ-01-034 speaks only of a caller who 'submits an empty country'; it does not say an absent key is a submission. The member write chose the opposite reading and recorded it in the code — members.service.ts, the wantsCountry branch: 'the key's presence — not its value — decides'. Left as a note because the screen always sends the key and the two routes differ in shape (a single-field PUT against a multi-field one), so nothing reachable through the product hits it.

notes.suggestedFix: either apply the same presence-decides rule here, or record in the contract that an absent key clears the column, so the difference between the two writes is a stated decision rather than a by-product of a shared validator

notes.rule: sweep 8 — the fixtures that pinned the dropped source were kept green rather than made discriminating
notes.symbol: a BY holiday appears for a BY member on Amounts Owed
notes.claim: the two country-sensitive reports suites were adapted by seeding Membership.countryCode equal to the phoneCountryCode already there, so no test in either suite can fail if reports.service.ts regressed to reading Account.phoneCountryCode

witness.detail: Each of those three members is now created with both phoneCountryCode: 'BY'|'US' and countryCode: 'BY'|'US' at the same value (amounts-owed 583-584 and 618-619; time-off 418-419). Before this diff the phone column was the only source and the fixture pinned it; after it, both sources resolve to the identical value, so every assertion holds under either implementation. Reverting resolveMemberHolidayCountry(m.countryCode, caller.organizationCountryCode) at apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts:1062 and :560 to the old phone read leaves all three cases green. The equivalent witness does exist for the holidays route — TC-01-INT-29 states PL on the membership while the account carries BY — but the contracts' call-site table names three reports call sites as well, and specs/time-off/README.md names Amounts Owed as the surface where this rule moves money. A note rather than a blocker because the document numbers no case for the reports adoption.

notes.suggestedFix: in the two reports suites, either drop phoneCountryCode from the fixtures that now state a membership country, or give the phone column a different country so the case fails if the phone read returns

notes.rule: sweep 8 — a branch of a stated rule has no assertion
notes.symbol: TC-01-UNIT-02: the range rules and the window presets
notes.claim: REQ-01-014 refuses a value that 'is not an ISO calendar date' and the implementation carries a dedicated isCalendarDate guard for it, but no case exercises a malformed or impossible date

witness.detail: The file asserts only the absent-endDate branch (line 17). isCalendarDate at packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts:74-83 additionally rejects '2026-13-01', '2026-02-30' and 'yesterday' by round-tripping through Date.UTC; deleting that round-trip leaves every assertion in the describe block green. The document's own steps for TC-01-UNIT-02 name only the missing endDate, so this is a gap in the case rather than an unimplemented rule.

notes.suggestedFix: add one assertion for a syntactically valid but impossible date, e.g. '2026-02-30' returning rangeRequired

notes.rule: sweep 8 — a comment claims coverage the case does not provide
notes.claim: the new doc comment says the phone country is left in place 'so the case also witnesses that it reaches nothing', but the only case that keeps a phone country sets the membership country to the same value and so witnesses nothing of the kind

witness.test: holidays.spec.ts TC-03-INT-14, 'scope=mine resolves the caller country server-side and ignores ?country'
witness.detail: The Belarusian member at apps/api/test/holidays.spec.ts:410-415 is created with phoneCountryCode: 'BY' and countryCode: 'BY', so the expected ['Labour Day','Victory Day'] holds whether HolidaysService reads the membership column or the account's phone column. notes.rule: TC-01-E2E-03's Expected Result — 'seven under the week preset, starting on the caller's firstDayOfWeek'
notes.symbol: picking four people holds through every window preset and step
notes.claim: the implemented TC-01-E2E-03 asserts only the day-header counts and never which weekday the window starts on, so the screen's wiring of session.account.firstDayOfWeek into timeOffCalendarWindowRange is asserted nowhere

witness.detail: Lines 257-276 assert toHaveCount(14) and toHaveCount(7) on [data-testid^="calendar-day-header-"], and the range label is only compared to itself across steps. If CalendarScreen.tsx:86-87 passed a constant instead of session.account.firstDayOfWeek, both counts would still be 14 and 7 and the case would pass. The computation itself is covered at unit level, which exercises Monday and Sunday against timeOffCalendarWindowRange, so what is uncovered is only the screen reading the preference.

notes.claim: the loading state is a bare Preloader rather than the skeleton of header rows plus six member rows the UI Description names, and unlike the shipped precedent it carries no role="status" and no accessible name

witness.detail: contracts §UI Description: 'Loading | The grid area holds a skeleton of the header rows plus six member rows; the filter bar stays interactive'. The second half holds — the filter bar sits outside the loading ternary — but CalendarScreen.tsx:333 renders <Preloader /> with no wrapper, no role and no aria-label. The app's shipped answer for the same substitution wraps it: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/settings/holidays/page.tsx renders Preloader inside a role="status" node with an aria-label. Kept as a note because a loading indicator is implemented and the document itself declines to test this state ('No case: the skeleton lives between two paints').

notes.suggestedFix: wrap the loader as the Holidays page does, with role="status" and an accessible name

notes.rule: CLAUDE.md — Validation: message text lives in packages/validation and is not spelled twice
notes.symbol: picking teams draws their union, and unticking the last one refuses without clearing
notes.claim: the banner assertion hardcodes 'Choose at least one team.' although the same file imports TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES and uses it for the empty-state title

witness.detail: Lines 210-212 assert toHaveText('Choose at least one team.') while line 2 imports TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES and line 365 uses TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.emptyStateTitle for the same kind of assertion. TC-01-E2E-02's Expected Result names the export, not the string: 'draws calendar-error-banner carrying TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.teamsRequired'. notes.rule: CLAUDE.md — Design system: no hardcoded colors or sizes
notes.claim: the organization-country control is wrapped in style={{ minWidth: 220 }} — a size literal carried by no token and recorded in no DS gap

witness.detail: page.tsx:360, <div style={{ minWidth: 220 }}>. The spec's DS gaps table records three gaps — the band colours, --name-col: 264px and the 3px band margin — and no width for this control. notes.rule: REQ-01-009 — an empty selection is a refusal, not everyone
notes.claim: the Teams and People pickers inherit MultiFilter's placeholder 'All', so the control reads 'All' in exactly the state REQ-01-009 refuses

witness.detail: apps/web/src/reports/ReportFilters.tsx sets placeholder="All" on the Select that MultiFilter draws, and CalendarScreen.tsx:276 and :289 pass no override. On the reports screens 'All' is correct because an unticked filter means every row; here an unticked selection is refused with teamsRequired or peopleRequired (REQ-01-009), so the placeholder states the opposite of the rule the banner beside it enforces. notes.rule: contracts §DS gaps — 'Each row says what ships in its place — a name the mock declares in its own :root, or a literal marked @literal where there is no name to declare'
notes.claim: the DS gaps table records the 3px band margin as a literal but not the 2px today-marker inset, which the spec's own mock carries and which the implementation copies faithfully

witness.detail: apps/web/app/globals.css:1104 writes box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 0 var(--action-primary) for the today column marker. It is the only size literal added by this change that is neither a 1px hairline (17 pre-existing occurrences in the same file) nor recorded in the DS gaps table nor marked @literal. It is not improvised: specs/time-off/01-vacation-calendar.mock.html:153 declares '.cell.today{box-shadow:inset 2px 0 0 0 var(--action-primary)}' verbatim, and the mock is the spec's stated visual acceptance target — so the code follows the document and the omission is the table's. Raised against the document rather than the code for that reason. The @media (max-width: 1199px) at globals.css:968 was checked and dismissed: a CSS media query cannot read a custom property, --layout-breakpoint-desktop is 1200px (packages/ds/src/tokens/spacing.css:35), and the identical query already ships at globals.css:554.

notes.suggestedFix: add the today marker's 2px inset to the DS gaps table as a fourth row, marked @literal beside the 3px band margin it sits next to

notes.claim: the settled Validation Rule 9 refuses three codes the picker the spec tells both screens to reuse still offers, so a control offers a value its own save cannot store. Planned, not halted on: the document nowhere states that every option must be storable, so both statements hold and the choice is a plan's to make.

witness.detail: An admin opens Settings > Holidays, picks 'Ascension Island' in org-country-select and clicks org-country-save. The option exists because HOLIDAY_COUNTRY_OPTIONS (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/settings/holidays/country-options.ts:17) is built from COUNTRY_OPTIONS (apps/web/src/account-data.ts:58), which is libphonenumber's getCountries(). Rule 9 now tests membership of COUNTRY_NAMES (packages/validation/src/autofill.ts:717), which does not carry AC. Counted: getCountries() returns 245 codes, COUNTRY_NAMES carries 249, and exactly AC, TA and XK are offered but not assigned. Before 40eedaa all three saved; after it all three answer 422 PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid. The same three reach member-country-select, which builds its list from the same array (MemberDetailScreen.tsx:42).

notes.suggestedFix: planned in T8 - both country Selects list only options the assigned-list test accepts, while the holiday form's picker and the holiday list's country filter keep the full list. If the document wants to say which list each country control offers, that is one sentence in Screens.

notes.claim: neither the requirements nor the contracts say what an absent countryCode key means on either country write, and the two routes have been given opposite answers by their shipped implementations

witness.detail: PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country with body {} today clears Organization.countryCode (organization-country.service.ts:69 hands undefined to the validator, which normalizes it to null and writes it). PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/members/{memberId} with no countryCode key deliberately leaves Membership.countryCode alone (members.service.ts:451, the 'countryCode' in input idiom). REQ-01-034 is triggered by 'submits an empty country' and REQ-01-042 by 'submits an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country'; neither says what submitting nothing at all does. No case in the bundle sends a body without the key to either route, so nothing observes the difference.

notes.suggestedFix: planned in T4 and T5 with both rules stated and the reason for the asymmetry - the organization route is a one-field settings resource whose GET and PUT carry the same representation, the member route carries three fields and a caller that ignores the new one must change nothing. A sentence in the contracts would settle it for good.

notes.claim: the document assigns no message to a calendar read that does not complete, and the screen must say something

witness.detail: The Error Messages table routes seven strings to the endpoint's 422s and gives emptyStateBody, emptyStateTitle, orgCountryHint and memberCountryDefaultOption no route at all; the UI Description's only failure row is 'Refused (422)', and the required-testid table describes calendar-error-banner as 'present on any 422'. A fetch that rejects, or a 500, is described by no row - which is how the first implementation came to draw 'No active member matches this scope.' over a populated grid.

notes.suggestedFix: planned in T7 with HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError, the string the Holidays page this same change edits already uses for a failed read. If the calendar should carry a message of its own, it is a row in the Error Messages table and a line in the UI Description.
